column1: # haiku2u content file — edit me freely!
# One row per candidate line:  theme
#   stage 1 = first line of the haiku  (5 syllables)
# A theme needs at least 3 lines per stage to appear in the game.
# Give a theme MORE than 3 lines per stage and the game will pick 3 at random.
# Lines may contain commas; only the first two commas split the row.
# Check your syllable counts with:  npm run check:syllables

column3: Shadows grow teeth in the dusk
The heart drums against its cage
What waits where the light cannot
Through winter the pine stays green
A vow carved deep into oak
A thousand small blows then light
The salmon leaps the white falls
Tides have carved this cliff for years
Bamboo bends and does not break
No footprints cross this white field
Smoke rises from one far hut
Geese write their V across dusk
Each beam raised by many backs
Old pines lean on each other
Words are not needed to sit
The sparrows feed their loud nest
Old roots new branches one tree
The bridge is mine to repair
Rain or not the fields need me
What the bones know the mouth hides
The plain stone outlasts the paint
The mask smiles while the eyes count
The cracked bowl shown not hidden
What I owe I say out loud
The tide reaches for the moon
Roots crawl for water all night
One lantern pulls all the moths
I plant for those I won't meet
The empty chair still leans back
The scar recalls the sharp day
Knees shake; the step happens still
The sprout dares the late spring frost
Fear walks with me not ahead
Even ash feeds the next spring
Far off the rain has ended
The seed believes in the sun
The willow learned how to weep
His coat still hangs by the door
Winter stays long in some rooms
The dog runs for the running
Sun warms the back of my neck
The vine and the trellis hold
I learn the weather of you
The orchard gave its last fruit
Where the tree stood so much sky
The song ends mid-verse and stays
What was map is now water
New banks for the same current
Even the dust here is mine
The road bends to one lit door
Each pass reveals one more pass
I trade my roof for the stars
The road eats months like berries
The river ran a wrong red
No side wins the burned harvest
The hawk lets the rabbit pass
A debt erased with one nod
Strong hands choosing to be soft
Ask the river how to yield
Old scars teach the new soldiers
New leaves drunk on their first rain
The whole map not yet unrolled
Trees I planted now shade me
Winter sun is still the sun
The word I swallowed still burns
The boat I watched from the shore
I set the heavy sack down
The bridge rebuilt plank by plank
Old wounds aired heal in sunlight
The kite string cut — and then sky
The bamboo spends years on roots
Fruit ripens at its own pace
Stone steps worn by soft slippers
What the fog does to the town
Even my thoughts take off shoes
The loudest part of the shrine
Night folds its dark laundry up
Gold spills over the ridge top
The kettle and the sky sing
Day signs its name in long shade
The fields exhale their stored heat
Lamps bloom one by one in town
The harvest moon weighs the fields
Green riots out of the thaw
The orchard holds its pink breath
The garden drinks past its fill
The pond seals its bright letter
Unseen yet it moves the world
Where light is I am also
It asks nothing and gives all
Each voice leaves room for the next
The geese agree on their V
Stones set just so in the stream
The night plants what day buried
In sleep the mute fish all sing
The burned hill wears new velvet
